REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy_With_Immunofluorescence

The combination of tense blisters and mucosal ulcers, especially with a family history of autoimmune disease, strongly suggests Bullous Pemphigoid, so I need to confirm this with a biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Acantholysis and intraepidermal blister formation. Direct Immunofluorescence: Intercellular IgG and C3 deposition within the epidermis. Autoantibodies: Presence of desmoglein antibodies. (Note: These findings are diagnostic of Pemphigus Vulgaris, characterized by flaccid blisters and a positive Nikolsky sign, rather than Bullous Pemphigoid).

speaker: Doctor
text: "I apologize for the earlier confusion; your biopsy confirms Pemphigus Vulgaris, which explains the mucosal ulcers and blistering despite the tense appearance you described. Given the confirmed diagnosis and your recent captopril use, are you currently experiencing any difficulty swallowing or breathing due to the throat ulcers?"
